messages:
maria: Heads up — started seeing intermittent Trivy failures on scan-orch that line up with the RBAC role changes last night. KMS decrypt errors + a bunch of duplicate retry uploads to S3. Impacting infra/* repos and causing suppression mapping to miss. Anyone on that shift?

ci-bot: [automated] scan-job failed for infra/edge-sdk at 2026-03-19T22:13:02Z
```
[2026-03-19 22:13:02] ERROR scan-worker: kms:Decrypt failed: AccessDenied: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef01
repo=infra/edge-sdk attempt=3
upload s3://redwood-scans/2026/03/19/infra-edge-sdk-commit-abc123.tar.gz failed -> queued retry
```

sam: @maria I'm looking. First guess: role used by scan-worker lost kms:Decrypt or the key policy now restricts to a principal that changed. Can you paste the failing role ARN and full KMS key id? Also check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt denied entries.

maria: role arn:aws:iam::123456:role/scan-worker-prod, key id = abcd-ef01. CloudTrail shows Deny for sts:AssumeRole -> then kms:Decrypt denied. We rolled a small infra RBAC tweak (narrowed assume-role principals) last night.

alex: Two related symptoms here: 1) KMS decrypt denies -> scan can't read cached artifacts -> worker retries and uploads new objects   2) suppression mapping currently matches by artifact key, so retries produce a different key and suppressions don't apply -> noisy vuln churn.

sam: Quick checks/commands:
```
aws sts get-caller-identity --profile scan-worker
aws s3api get-object-acl --bucket redwood-scans --key "2026/03/19/.../infra-edge-sdk-commit-abc123.tar.gz"
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group /aws/lambda/scan-worker --filter-pattern "kms:Decrypt" --start-time 1710000000000
```

anya: For immediate mitigation we should NOT create new suppression entries on failed scans. Also add a dedupe key for suppression that is stable across retries (repo+commit+scanner-version) instead of S3 object path. That will avoid losing mapping when uploads get rekeyed.

leo: Also we need to triage the CVE noise — we've got a handful of high sev findings that are real. Proposed quick priority buckets: P0 = prod-exploitable (patch within 24h), P1 = high but behind mitigations (7d), P2 = non-prod or low-exposure (30d). Assign owners: infra-security for infra/* P0/P1, app teams for app/* P1/P2.

alex: Agreed. Short-term actions:
- Devops: revert or widen the assume-role principals to include the scan-worker role (sam)
- Security: switch suppression dedupe to repo+commit+scanner-version and pause repo-scoped suppression for infra/* (maria/anya)
- CI: re-run backlog with corrected role and dedupe (ci-bot)
- Product/security: run triage on the top 10 high sev CVEs and mark P0/P1 (leo)

sam: IAM policy snippet that usually fixes kms:Decrypt issues (add to the role's inline policy or ensure key policy allows this principal):
```
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [
    {
      "Effect": "Allow",
      "Action": ["kms:Decrypt"],
      "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456:key/abcd-ef01",
      "Principal": { "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456:role/scan-worker-prod" }
    }
  ]
}
```

anya: Also add instrumentation: emit a metric when a suppression lookup misses so we can alert on suppression churn. That will help detect noisy retries vs real new artifacts.

maria: I'll widen the assume-role principal for the scan-worker role temporarily and toggle off repo-scoped suppression for infra/* now. Re-running backlog with a controlled window. I'll post PRs and the run link here. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: queued 58 backlog scans for infra/* after role update (eta ~18m)

leo: I'll start the CVE triage doc and ping app owners for the top 3 libs.

sam: after we stabilise, we should deploy a small reconciler that maps suppression keys by stable id (repo+commit+scanner) and optionally garbage-collect old S3-stored artifacts to avoid key explosion.

maria: thanks all — will follow up with PR links and the triage spreadsheet in the morning. If anyone sees more kms:Decrypt denies in CloudTrail ping me directly.
